Terminal Tree — the Tree Is the Tiling

Features·seedling·proposed·JUL 29, 2026

One tree of first-class terminals; canvas layout, Dock rows and focus all derive from it. The redesign that makes #2059-class invisibility unrepresentable — in three phases, TR1–TR3.

Contents

  • The model — layout is a function of the tree
  • Why — the class behind #2059
  • The phase tree — TR1‥TR3
    • TR1 — focus = camera
    • TR2 — every terminal a tile
    • TR3 — depth legalized
  • Composing with terminal-teams

The design, in one sentence: the tree is the tiling. Every terminal is a node in one tree (padi’s existing parentId) and a first-class tile on the canvas; default placement is a pure function of the tree (children tile beside their parent, arrows draw the edges), dragging overrides one tile, focus is the camera zooming to a tile, and the Dock is the same tree walked as rows. No splits, no sub-panel, no maximized mode, no “Autoarrange” action — auto-arrangement is the resting state, not a command.

The model — layout is a function of the tree

  • Every terminal is a tile. An agent teammate, a just dev, a lazygit — same thing, differing only in size and parent. There is no second kind of terminal (no split, no sub-tab, no “stuck” attachment), so there is no second rendering path.
  • Default placement is f(tree) — deterministic and total: each child tiles in a column to the right of its parent, siblings stack, subtrees space by their extent.The concrete default: place a child at parent.x + parent.w + gutter, stacking siblings top-to-bottom in tree order; a subtree reserves the vertical extent of its descendants. Helpers (terminals with no agent) get the compact tile size. Any deterministic packer with these properties is acceptable; the property that matters is total — every node gets coordinates. Edges render as arrows between tiles; relation labels on the arrows come from terminal-teams F2 when that lands, not from this design.
  • Drag wins, per tile. Dragging a tile flags it layoutMode: "manual" in its existing canvasLayout; everything else keeps flowing from the tree. There is deliberately no Autoarrange command to press or to accidentally destroy a hand layout with — auto is simply what a tile does until a human moves it.
  • Focus = camera. “Maximize” is the camera zooming until a tile fills the viewport (~200 ms tween, instant under reduced-motion); Esc or a background click flies back. Focusing a tile that has children fits its subtree, not just the tile — main terminal large, helpers visible beside it — which is exactly the job the maximized sub-panel does today. Same scene, same renderer — the maximized mode (useViewPosture, covered tiles, dock-posture split) is deleted. A Dock row click teleports the camera to that tile.

Why — the class behind #2059

#2059: a terminal created over MCP with a parentId that is itself a split child is fully alive in padi but never renders — the client derives tiles by filtering (!parentId → tile, one level of children per tile) and a grandchild matches no rule, so it silently has zero render sites.The mechanism: useTerminalMetadata.ts keeps records with no parentId as tiles; children are looked up only per-tile in TerminalContent.tsx. A depth-2 record is excluded from both. Session restore has a second latent instance of the same class — its two-level partition drops a grandchild whose parent appears later in the saved array (sessionRestore.ts). The class of bug: when visibility is derived by filtering, anything that matches no rule disappears without an error.

This design deletes the class instead of the instance: placement is a total function (every node gets coordinates), rendering is a full tree walk (never a filter), and TR3 adds the belt-and-braces totality assert — every active, non-parked terminal has exactly one render site, else a loud error.A stopgap guard (#2060) that rejects nested parentId at create is in flight independently of this plan. The plan assumes nothing about it: if it lands first, TR3 deletes the guard; if it doesn’t, there is nothing to delete. Either way depth becomes legal input only at TR3.

The phase tree — TR1‥TR3

TR1 — focus = camera

Replace maximized mode with zoom-to-tile: double-click / shortcut flies the camera to fit the tile; a tile with children gets a subtree fit — the camera frames the parent plus its (still-split, at this phase) tile; Esc flies back; Dock click teleports; useViewPosture, covered-tile rendering and the dock-posture split are deleted; xterm re-renders at native pixels when the camera settles. User-visible delta: maximize becomes a smooth zoom that keeps the fleet one gesture away; behavior is otherwise equivalent. Acceptance: double-click a tile → it fills the viewport crisply; Esc → back to the fleet at the previous camera; click a Dock row while zoomed → camera flies to that tile; grep confirms the posture module is gone. Why first: TR2 retires the split sub-panel, and the camera’s subtree fit is its functional replacement — a focused parent must already be able to show its helpers beside it, or TR2 would strand maximized workflows with no way to see a dev server while working.

TR2 — every terminal a tile

The rendering rewrite: retire the in-tile split/sub-panel UI; existing parentId children become their own (compact) tiles, auto-placed beside their parent with edges drawn; dragging a tile pins it manually.The split button’s behavior is unchanged from the user’s view: it still creates a child terminal; the child now appears as an adjacent tile rather than a pane. User-visible delta: sub-terminals appear as adjacent connected tiles instead of panes inside the parent — and in a focused view, focusing the parent frames the subtree (TR1), so the “maximized terminal with its dev server visible” workflow survives the sub-panel’s removal unchanged. Acceptance: create a sub-terminal from a tile → it renders as its own tile beside the parent with an arrow; drag it → it stays where dropped; reload → both facts survive; focus the parent → the camera frames parent + children together. Why separate: it is sequenced on TR1 (the subtree-fit camera must exist before the sub-panel goes) and must itself land before depth is legal input (TR3) — legalizing nested parentId while the split UI is still the renderer would recreate #2059’s unrenderable records.

The types already carry the design — TR2 is mostly deleting schema, not adding it. The one semantic change: canvasLayout present ⇔ manually placed; absent means the position is derived. No layoutMode enum, no override knob.

// padi/src/chromeVocab.ts — shape unchanged; meaning sharpened:
// stored only once a human drags the tile. Absent ⇒ position = f(tree).
export const CanvasLayoutSchema = z.object({ x: z.number(), y: z.number(), w: z.number(), h: z.number() });

export const SubPanelStateSchema = z.object({ collapsed: z.boolean(), panelSize: z.number() });
// ⟵ DELETED in TR2, with its `subPanel` field below — the sub-panel UI it describes is retired.

// padi/src/vocab.ts · ClientPersistedTerminalFieldsSchema — the fields TR2 touches:
{
  parentId: z.string().optional(),                //  THE tree — already on the wire, unchanged
  canvasLayout: CanvasLayoutSchema.optional(),    //  present ⇔ manual pin (was: always written)
  subPanel: SubPanelStateSchema.optional(),       //  ⟵ DELETED (and from SavedTerminal/restore)
}

// padi/src/surface.ts — creation input is already sufficient; TR2 changes nothing here.
export const PadiCreateInputSchema = z.object({ cwd: z.string().optional(), parentId: TerminalIdSchema.optional() })
  .merge(CreateTerminalInputSchema);

// client — the new piece is one pure function, no wire type at all:
//   total: every active record gets a box; manual pins pass through, the rest derive.
layoutTree(records: TerminalMetadata[]): Map<TerminalId, { x; y; w; h }>

Migration falls out of the semantics: legacy top-level tiles all have a saved canvasLayout, so they load as manual pins (nobody’s hand layout moves); today’s splits have none, so they auto-tile on first render. Saved subPanel state is dropped on load — the UI it configured no longer exists.

TR3 — depth legalized

Make nested parentId legal input end to end: delete the create-time nesting guard if the stopgap (#2060) landed; make the Dock recursive (arbitrary-depth indented rows, relation chip); fix session restore’s order-dependent two-level partition by restoring via tree walk; add the totality assert (every active terminal has exactly one render site — loud error, per the fail-fast rule). User-visible delta: an agent can parent a terminal under any terminal; the chain renders as cascading tiles and nested Dock rows. Acceptance: over MCP, create a depth-2 chain (the #2059 repro) → both terminals render as tiles, the Dock shows depth-2 indentation, no error anywhere; restart kolu → the chain survives. Why separate: it is sequenced on TR2 — rendering must be total before depth becomes legal input; Dock recursion and the restore fix ride along because they are the same tree walk.

Composing with terminal-teams

terminal-teams F1–F4 predate this note; the fit is clean but two items change shape. F1 (create --near) is superseded by TR2’s automap — placement no longer needs a flag because it is derived; F1 should not be built. F2 (typed relations) and F3 (edges + badges) compose: this design draws containment edges from parentId; F2’s delegates | consults | reviews become labels/badges on those arrows (and Dock chips) rather than a second edge system — the footnote in terminal-teams that keeps parentId separate from relations (“containment ≠ collaboration”) holds unchanged. F4 (/goal) is orthogonal.
